questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to ﬁll in the blank and make a grammatically correct sentence.**

It was ______ honour for Seema to be selected as a teacher trainer.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

__Article **'****an' **is used before vowels a, e, i, o, u. It is also used before consonants which have vowel-like sound.__

Eg: *an honest, an FIR, etc*

Other options are therefore incorrect to use in the context.

The sentence would thus be: *It was __an__ honour for Seema to be selected as a teacher trainer. *

questions.question:
Direction: In the following question, out of the four alternatives, select the alternative which will improve the underlined part of the sentence. In case no improvement is needed, select “No improvement”.

Tommy's eyes grew wide __on a sight of__ the new bicycle.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **at the sight of**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• The preposition **'on' **is used incorrectly It must be replaced with the preposition **'at'.**
 
• The phrase **at the sight of **means upon seeing.

 **Example: **He faints** at the sight of** blood.

 

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Tommy's eyes grew wide at the sight of__ the new bicycle. *

questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate option to substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence. If there is no need to substitute it, select No improvement.**

__It has been announcing__ that the bus will be late by an hour.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

'It has been announcing' is used incorrectly.

**'has been'** denotes that the sentence is in the __present perfect tense__. It is used to indicate completed activities in the immediate past.

Thus, '**announced**' must be replaced with **'announcing'.**

Thus the correct sentence will be: *It has been announced that the bus will be late by an hour.*

questions.question:
**Identify the segment in the sentence which contains the grammatical error. **

Seema was sprinkled the cashews over the pie to garnish it.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3.**

The error lies in the 1st part of the sentence **'Seema was sprinkled'.**

The verb 'was' must be replaced with present perfect tense **'has'.**

__The present perfect tense is used to express past actions whose time is not given and not definite.__

Thus the correct sentence will be: *Seema has sprinkled the cashews over the pie to garnish it.*

questions.question:
Which two signs need to be interchanged to make the given equation correct?

27 - 3 × 2 ÷ 13 + 9 = 14
questions.solution:
1) ×, ÷

Given equation: 27 - 3 x 2 ÷ 13 + 9 = 14

After interchanging the signs ‘×, ÷’, we get:

L.H.S = 27 - 3 ÷ 2 × 13 + 9

= 27 - 1.5 × 13 + 9

= 27 - 19.5 + 9

= 36 - 19.5

= 16.5 ≠ R.H.S

**2) -, ÷**

**Given equation: 27 - 3 × 2 ÷ 13 + 9 = 14**

**After interchanging the signs ‘-, ÷’, we get:**

**L.H.S = 27 ÷ 3 × 2 - 13 + 9**

**= 9 × 2 - 13 + 9**

**= 18 - 13 + 9**

**= 27 - 13**

**= 14 = R.H.S**

3) -, ×

Given equation: 27 - 3 × 2 ÷ 13 + 9 = 14

After interchanging the signs ‘-, ×’, we get:

L.H.S = 27 × 3 - 2 ÷ 13 + 9

= 81 - 0.15 + 9

= 90 - 0.15

= 89.85 ≠ R.H.S

4) ÷, +

Given equation: 27 - 3 × 2 ÷ 13 + 9 = 14

After interchanging the signs ‘÷, +’, we get:

L.H.S = 27 - 3 × 2 + 13 ÷ 9

= 27 - 6 + 1.4

= 28.4 - 6

= 22.4 ≠ R.H.S

Hence, ‘-, ÷’ is the correct answer

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of a mother and a son is 4 : 1 Fourteen years from now, the ratio of their ages will be 2 : 1. The present age (in years) of the mother is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Equate the **ratio difference** by making the **age gap** constant between the mother and son.

Present Ratio = 4 : 1 (Gap = 3 units) | Future Ratio (after 14 years) = 2 : 1 (Gap = 1 unit).

Multiply the future ratio by 3 to equalize gaps: Future Ratio = 6 : 3.

Increase in units for Mother = 6 − 4 = 2 units → 2 units = 14 years → 1 unit = 7 years.

Present age of **Mother** = 4 units × 7 = 28 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present age ratio (Mother : Son) = **4 : 1**

Ratio after 14 years = **2 : 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/bd113e833a9597809bd493e87888c098fd74b956f1f79288f210d6ef5a9e3295.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the present age of the **Mother** be 4x and the **Son** be x.

⇒ According to the question, after 14 years:

⇒ (4x + 14) / (x + 14) = 2 / 1

⇒ 4x + 14 = 2 × (x + 14)

⇒ 4x + 14 = 2x + 28

⇒ 4x − 2x = 28 − 14

⇒ 2x = 14

⇒ x = 7

⇒ Present age of Mother = 4x = 4 × 7 = 28 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 28 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The numerical difference between the ages of two persons **always remains constant**, regardless of how many years pass.

Ratio Balancing Method

To solve age problems quickly, multiply the ratios by the **difference of the other ratio** to ensure the unit change is consistent with the time elapsed.

Cross-Product Method

For a ratio a:b becoming c:d after x years, use the formula: 1 unit = [x × (c − d)] / [(a × d) − (b × c)].</p

questions.question: A, B and C can do a work in 12, 15 and 20 days respectively. In how many days, working together they can complete the same work?
questions.solution:

Total work = Efficiency × Time taken

**Calculation:**

Total work = 60 units (LCM of 12, 15, 20)

⇒ Efficiency of A = 60/12 = 5 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of B = 60/15 = 4 units/day

⇒ Efficiency of C = 60/20 = 3 units/day

∴ A, B and C together complete the whole work in = 60/(5 + 4 + 3) = 60/12 = 5 days.

Average speed = Total distance covered/Total time taken

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

questions.question: Image formed by Plane Mirror is always ________.
questions.solution:
__CONCEPT:__

__
 
• Plane Mirror: A plane mirror is a mirror with a flat (planar) reflective surface.

The characteristics of an image formed in a plane mirror:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13ff2a7e1be1cb854b8dd08c9c6ab537716e1426fe3d497995587e5c7304852.png] 

 
• The image formed by the plane mirror is virtual and erect i.e. image cannot be projected or focused on a screen.
 
• The distance of the image ‘behind’ the mirror is the same as the distance of the object in front of the mirror.
 
• The size of the image formed is the same as the size of the object.
 
• The image is laterally inverted, i.e. left hand appears to be right hand when seen from the plane mirror.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3d092687faf74746b566b59e1e432f1ba5504516fa974143e619ab92dbc19c55.png] 

 
• If the object moves towards (or away from) the mirror at a certain rate, the image also moves towards (or away from) the mirror at the same rate.

EXPLANATION__:

From the above discussion, we can say that,

 
• The **image formed by Plane Mirror is always** **Virtual and Erect. **So option 1 is correct.
 
• A **convex lens and a concave mirror** forms both real and virtual images.
 
• A **concave lens and a convex mirror** can form only virtual images.

questions.question: "Any body that is completely or partially submerged in a ﬂuid (gas or liquid) at rest is acted upon by an upward or buoyant force, the magnitude of which is equal to the weight of the ﬂuid displaced by the body." Which is this law?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Archimedes' Principle**__

__Concept:__

Archimedes principle:

__
 
• The principle of Archimedes states “When a body is immersed in a liquid, an upward thrust, equal to the weight of the liquid displaced, acts on it.”

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/965af0fe078d8cd5de7d0224fb4dbf687b4efa01717a8d927db4a1b4462666bc.png] 

 
• Thus, when a solid is fully immersed in a liquid, it loses weight which is equal to the weight of the liquid it displaces.

Apparent weight = Actual weight - boyant force = mg - ρgV

Where m is mass of the object, ρ is the density of the fluid 

Hence if there is no gravity, there is no Upward Thrust.

The upward force applied to the object is called the buoyant force.

Here,

ρ = density of liquid

g = acceleration due to gravity

V = volume of liquid displaced by the object

questions.question: The Narrow Zone of contact between land, air and water is called ________.
questions.solution:
__
 
• The Narrow Zone of contact between land, air and water is called **Biosphere**__.
 
• There are three types of biospheres, as the lithosphere, hydrosphere and atmosphere.
 
• The lithosphere is the rocky outer part of the Earth.
 
• The hydrosphere is the total amount of water present on a planet.
 
• The layers of gases around the earth completely form the atmosphere.
